attrs.evidence: cas.mjs (artifactRoot over the parsed object; resolveArtifact re-deriving the root and naming all four outcomes), nest_bundle.mjs, nest_check.mjs -- whose child table, connectives, scope, grammar and chain derivation are each declared inside it and NOT imported, for the fifth round running -- and nest_forgeries.mjs; gate `gov-nest`. THE SHIPPED DAG is D = C2 AND C1, C2 = C1 AND A, C1 = A AND B: a diamond twice over, whose shared node is deliberately the 1.3 MB P1 bundle because a diamond over a cheap node measures nothing. A 4,518-byte artifact names 3,620,908 bytes of proof: 8 citations over 4 distinct artifacts, 1,266,802 bytes stored once (2.86x), 8 child-checker invocations of which 4 re-verify bytes already accepted, depth 3, and 404 films replayed TRANSITIVELY against 0 replayed by the parent -- structural, because nest_check.mjs directly imports no kernel, no emitter, no decoder and not the derivation protocol's encoder either. nest_forgeries.mjs 26/26 across 14 refusal codes. The headline forgery is an artifact with nothing wrong with it: every root re-derives, every certificate recomputes, every aggregate reseals, every address resolves -- over a child its own checker refuses. Grid probes are behavioural and synthesise their own store; disabling the root re-derivation in cas.mjs flips exactly one of the five reported booleans.
attrs.statement: IDENTITY, AVAILABILITY and WARRANT are three things, and a content address supplies the first two only. A content hash says WHICH artifact is meant; a store says WHERE its bytes are; that it was ACCEPTED is neither, and may be established only by running the checker of the artifact's own protocol -- on every citation, including one whose bytes this run has already accepted. A RESOLVING VERIFIER MUST RE-DERIVE THE ADDRESS FROM THE BYTES IT RECEIVED, and over the PARSED OBJECT rather than the received octets, so that what it authenticated and what it reasons about cannot be two different values. The store is untrusted by construction; the standing counter-example is an INPUT-addressed action cache, whose key cannot validate its value, so a client must simply trust whoever wrote it. AND A CACHED VERDICT IS NOT A PROPERTY OF THE BYTES: it is a property of the bytes AND the checker AND its version, so issuing one is a verifier-owned authority decision and never a hash. Until such an authority exists the same artifact cited twice is CHECKED TWICE, and the gap between child_checker_invocations and unique_subtree_roots is the MEASURED price of not having issued a warrant rather than a cost avoided in silence. THERE IS A FOURTH THING AND IT COMES BEFORE THE OTHER THREE: CITABILITY. An artifact must carry the fields its citation identity binds, and measured against the shipped P3 artifact verifiedClaimSemId THREW `certificate-incomplete: chain_ids` -- so a composed certificate could not be NAMED at all, and P3's declared non-transitivity was a hole rather than a policy. A composition's chain is DERIVED from the children it resolved and may never be declared, which is law:proof.claimant-may-not-define-the-semantics one layer out. RECURSION TERMINATES BY A DECLARED DEPTH CEILING AND NOT BY AN APPEAL TO PREIMAGE RESISTANCE: a cycle cannot be sealed, measured over 512 attempted fixpoints with no convergence, so the cycle guard is declared DEFENCE IN DEPTH and not load-bearing -- but a long CHAIN is not a cycle, is perfectly constructible, and is refused at the shipped bound by a real witness rather than by a grep of the constant.
